provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Concedes a fact the speaker accepts as true, then reports that what you would expect from it did not follow, typically a shortfall, a doubt, or an unrealized result (頭では分かっているものの、実行できない). Its classmate かと思いきや instead reports surprise that reality contradicted an assumption. More written and deliberate than けれど or が. It follows a な-adjective with な (便利なものの) and a noun with である (事実であるものの).

examples.ruby: 頭[あたま]では分[わ]かっているものの、なかなか実行[じっこう]できない。
examples.english: I understand it well enough in my head, but I just can't put it into practice.

examples.ruby: 値段[ねだん]は高[たか]いものの、品質[ひんしつ]には文句[もんく]のつけようがない。
examples.english: It is expensive, but you can't fault the quality.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]はよく食[た]べるものの、少[すこ]しも太[ふと]らない。
examples.english: My little brother eats plenty, yet he never puts on any weight.

patterns.usage_note: Reports that reality contradicted what the speaker had assumed, with audible surprise (簡単な問題かと思いきや、解き方が分からない). The outcome is normally something already observed rather than a prediction. Its classmate ものの concedes a fact with no element of surprise. The base form is と思いきや, from classical 思ひきや, which keeps it slightly bookish; か is added after a noun or a question-like clause.

examples.ruby: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]るかと思[おも]いきや、空[そら]はすっかり晴[は]れ上[あ]がった。
examples.english: I was sure it would rain, and instead the sky cleared up completely.

examples.ruby: 簡単[かんたん]な問題[もんだい]かと思[おも]いきや、全然[ぜんぜん]解[と]き方[かた]が分[わ]からない。
examples.english: It looked like an easy problem, but I can't figure out how to solve it at all.

examples.ruby: 猫[ねこ]はもう寝[ね]たかと思[おも]いきや、押[お]し入[い]れの奥[おく]で暴[あば]れていた。
examples.english: I thought the cat had settled down for the night, but there she was tearing around the back of the closet.
